blocks.text: **The task.** Given a 2D grid, visit every cell in row-major order — left to right along row 0, then left to right along row 1, and so on — collecting the values into a flat list.
This is the traversal that matches the memory layout, so it is both the simplest to write and the fastest to run. Outer loop over rows, inner loop over columns.

items: `grid.length` is the number of **rows**, because the outer array holds rows.
`grid[r].length` is the number of **columns** in that row. Using it per-row rather than once is safer — it still works if rows have different lengths.
The inner loop varies `c`, which is what makes this row-major. Swapping the loops would produce column-major output.

blocks.text: **Time: O(R x C)** — every cell is visited exactly once, and there is no way to do better when the answer depends on every cell.
**Space: O(R x C)** for the output list. If you only needed to *process* each value rather than collect it, the extra space would be O(1).
This is the traversal you should reach for by default. Only deviate when a problem specifically demands a different order.
